page: Microsoft Azure D4ads_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dadv6 family, powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz and includes a cache hierarchy of 32 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, AVX512_BF16, and SHA_NI cryptography extensions.

The server is equipped with 16.0 GB of RAM, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per vCPU. It includes 236 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and is Premium Storage capable, though it does not bundle any complimentary public IPv4 addresses or GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. Text processing performance is also strong. However, multi-core performance, static web serving throughput, and image processing fall into average ranges. Memory read bandwidth is relatively weak, as are database operations and Redis SET throughput. LLM inference speeds are average for small 135M models but drop to poor or weak tiers for medium 7B models.

Given its balanced compute-to-memory ratio and local NVMe SSD, the D4ads_v6 offers a cost-effective profile for general-purpose workloads, light web serving, and single-threaded applications. It is less suited for memory-intensive databases, heavy multi-threaded decompression, or large-scale LLM inference.
